data.title: Unity Software upgraded at BofA after strong results
data.description:
• Unity Software (U) was in the spotlight on Friday after Bank of America upgraded the video game engine company to Buy from Neutral after it reported stronger-than-expected results this week. 
  • Shares rose 5.7% in premarket trading.
  • “We upgrade Unity to Buy from Neutral, as we now see a Vector growth runway sustainable through year-end CY27,” analyst Omar Dessousky wrote in a note to clients. “We view Unity Ads’ blowout quarter as an inflection point: it delivers the first financial validation that runtime data can power efficacy gains in Vector’s targeting model, reinforcing the narrative that Unity is following AppLovin’s path toward becoming another scaled user acquisition channel for mobile gaming advertisers. Only games built on Unity 6 (~30% of total) feed data into Vector today, and Unity is actively extending coverage to older titles. We expect a revisions cycle in Street 2H26 & CY27 estimates as 1) runtime data benefits continue to accrue, and 2) the scale of runtime data expands, unlocking further performance gains. 2Q beat driven by Vector blowout performance 2Q26 revenue ($547mn) landed well above the high end of guidance ($515mn).” 
  • In addition to the upgrade, Dessousky raised his price target on Unity to $50 from $30.

data.title: Omada health signals $334M-$340M 2026 revenue outlook while planning CEO transition on January 1, 2027
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Omada Health (OMDA) Q2 2026

Management View

  • “We just reported our strongest quarter ever, reaching a record number of members and our highest revenue and gross margin to date.” (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Sean Duffy)
  • “On January 1, 2027, Omada's President, Wei-Li Shao, will become the Chief Executive Officer,” and Duffy added, “I am equally excited to move into my new role as Executive Chair.” (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy)
  • “Year-over-year, we delivered 43% revenue growth and expanded gross margin by 700 basis points to 73% on a GAAP basis and by 600 basis points to 74% on a non-GAAP basis.” (President Wei-Li Shao)
  • “In Q2, we extended those programs into HCSC's fully insured book of business in three additional states, reaching an additional 1.5 million covered lives launching in 2027.” (President Shao)
  • “Q2 is the strongest second quarter in Omada's history,” and “we set quarterly records for revenue at $88 million… net income at $5 million, and adjusted EBITDA at $11 million.” (Chief Financial Officer Steven Cook)

Outlook

  • “We are raising full year revenue guidance to $334 million to $340 million, up from the prior guidance of $322 million to $330 million.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • “We're raising full year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $21 million to $27 million, up from prior guidance of $14 million to $20 million.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Cook said the raised outlook assumes “a more measured second half growth trajectory based on the historic seasonality and contracted visibility,” adding that “our year-over-year growth rate is expected to moderate in the second half” after “an exceptionally strong first half enrollment period.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • “At our Investor Day on September 10, we will lay out an updated long-term financial framework, including the growth, gross margin, and operating leverage trajectory.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)

Financial Results

  • Cook reported Q2 revenue of $88 million, GAAP gross margin of 73% (74% non-GAAP), GAAP net income of more than $5 million, and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $11 million; he also said the company ended Q2 with “cash and cash equivalents of approximately $222 million” and “no debt.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Cook introduced a new unit metric and said “trailing 12-month revenue per total member was $284 in Q2 compared with $279 in Q2 of last year,” while noting Omada “ended Q2 with approximately 1.1 million total members.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • On profitability drivers, Cook said gross margin expansion “reflects a lower cost to serve our members,” while operating leverage reflected “scaling through channel partnerships, getting more from our existing sales force, and tight spending discipline across the rest of the business.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)

Q&A

  • Craig Hettenbach, Morgan Stanley: Asked how AI efficiencies are flowing through and affecting headcount; Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy answered that AI is driving leverage “ranging from smarter tooling of our coaches… better prediction of member demand… MealMap and Omada Spark,” and he highlighted “the cost of revenue per member is down over 10%.” (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy)
  • Craig Hettenbach, Morgan Stanley: Asked what’s driving PBM channel strength; President Shao said Omada’s playbook centers on “partnering very, very closely with their sales teams,” plus “product market fit” in GLP-1s and “a suite of products… comprehensive across the cardiometabolic spectrum.” (President Shao)
  • Ryan MacDonald, Needham: Pressed that Omada is not “just a GLP-1 beneficiary”; President Shao said employers’ top cost concerns repeatedly include “cardiovascular disease, metabolic disease, obesity, diabetes,” and he positioned Omada as having “a full suite of cardiometabolic options” including cholesterol and “our prescribing program.” (President Shao)
  • Ryan MacDonald, Needham: Asked what’s embedded in the back-half revenue guide; Chief Financial Officer Cook said 2026 is “a more normal cadence” and emphasized comparisons to “a very strong 2025,” with last year’s back half “54%” revenue growth aided by channel ramping. (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Richard Close, Canaccord: Asked if GLP-1 employer coverage is cooling; President Shao said employers are still deciding and Omada sees “both those situations occurring,” arguing Omada is positioned for covered and non-covered scenarios via “prescribing plus wraparound GLP-1 support” and “GLP-1 FlexCare… and our partnership with the Lilly Employer Enterprise Connect program.” (President Shao)
  • Christopher Charlton, BMO: Asked why EBITDA margin implied moderation; Chief Financial Officer Cook said Q1 included front-loaded investments and “we hired roughly 50 people” with OpEx expected to “roughly hold flat if not tick up slightly in H2.” (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • David Larsen, BTIG: Asked about GLP-1 member mix and PBM reporting; President Shao said employer reporting includes deployment and outcomes (e.g., “Was their blood glucose controlled? Was their weight controlled? Was their blood pressure controlled?”), and Chief Financial Officer Cook said the GLP-1 ratio “has roughly held constant.” (President Shao; Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Ayush Vyas, Evercore: Asked when HCSC fully insured expansion hits revenue and whether the retailer cholesterol win was an upsell; President Shao said HCSC’s benefit-embedded structure is “a faster return,” with revenue “throughout H1 of next year,” and cholesterol at the large retailer was “an existing customer.” (President Shao)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts slightly positive, with repeated emphasis on durability beyond GLP-1s and on guidance conservatism; questions probed seasonality and implied margin step-down (e.g., BMO asked about “some moderation” in back-half margin). (Christopher Charlton, BMO Capital Markets Equity Research)
  • Management positive in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, repeatedly tying margin and efficiency to AI and execution; Duffy said AI is “starting to show up in the numbers,” and Cook framed guidance as seasonality plus investment cadence. (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy; Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Versus last quarter, management tone added a major leadership transition; Duffy said, “I'm ready to pass the leadership baton,” while positioning continuity via “Executive Chair.” (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy)

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q2 introduced a CEO succession timeline, with Shao named CEO effective January 1, 2027; Q1 emphasized new channel additions (Optum Rx Weight Engage and Lilly Employer Connect) without leadership change. (Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy)
  • Q2 guidance was raised again, moving from Q1’s $322 million-$330 million revenue outlook and $14 million-$20 million adjusted EBITDA outlook to $334 million-$340 million and $21 million-$27 million, respectively. (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Q2 messaging leaned more into “a more measured second half growth trajectory” and “growth rate… expected to moderate,” while Q1 highlighted “a guidance raise” alongside early traction in new partnerships. (Chief Financial Officer Cook; Co-Founder, CEO & Director Duffy)
  • Q2 expanded commercial narrative included HCSC’s fully insured expansion and cholesterol as a standalone track with a large retailer; Q1 focused on laying GLP-1 prescribing and benefit-design pathways, with revenue contribution from prescribing expected to build “more meaningfully in 2027.” (President Shao)

Risks and Concerns

  • President Shao said employer GLP-1 coverage decisions are mixed and still forming: “some… are considering expanding coverage… and some… are walking away,” adding “it's hard to predict… because everybody's just making their decisions right now.” (President Shao)
  • Chief Financial Officer Cook cautioned that expense and margin cadence reflects investment timing and seasonality, noting OpEx could “tick up slightly in H2” as the company hires and prepares for 2027. (Chief Financial Officer Cook)
  • Management repeatedly tied near-term growth patterns to enrollment seasonality, with Cook stating “Q1 remains our strongest enrollment period each year” and pointing to the “next significant enrollment inflection point” in the 2027 benefit cycle. (Chief Financial Officer Cook)

Final Takeaway

Omada’s management described Q2 as a record quarter with raised full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, while emphasizing that second-half growth is expected to moderate due to seasonality and investment cadence. The call also introduced a defined leadership transition, with President Wei-Li Shao set to become CEO on January 1, 2027 and current CEO Sean Duffy moving to Executive Chair. Commercially, management highlighted momentum across cardiometabolic programs and channels, including continued PBM progress, a 2027-covered-lives expansion with HCSC, and early demand signals for cholesterol and GLP-1-related offerings, with further long-term targets slated for an updated framework at the September 10 Investor Day.

data.title: TMX Group reports 36% jump in July trading value despite lower volumes
data.description:
• TMX Group (X:CA) (TMXXF) announced on Friday its July 2026 trading statistics, as trading value and transactions increased from a year earlier despite lower trading volumes.

  • Across all TMX equity marketplaces, trading value rose 36.6% YoY to $411.4B, while transactions increased 26.6% to 30.2M. 

  • Trading volume fell 7.5% to 12B shares.

  • On the Toronto Stock Exchange, trading value climbed 38.6% YoY to $392B, while trading volume rose 11.1% and transactions increased 27.5%.

  • TSX Venture Exchange trading value was $2.3B, up slightly from a year ago, while trading volume declined 36.1%.

  • Year-to-date, TMX's equity marketplaces reported 39.1% growth in trading value, 26.1% higher trading volume, and 33.9% more transactions than the same period last year.

data.title: CVRx forecasts 2026 revenue of $58M-$60M amid sales productivity and medicare advantage headwinds
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: CVRx (CVRX) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "We delivered total revenue of $15.7 million in the second quarter, demonstrating growth of 16% over the same quarter last year, with a gross margin of 87%." (President, CEO & Director Kevin Hykes)
  • "Despite the positive quarter, we are seeing signs that the back half of the year will not be as strong as the first. As a result, we've lowered our revenue guidance for the year." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • "This rapid pace of hiring has strained our onboarding and training processes" and management tied the guidance reset to "the scale of the turnover, the slower pace of the territory manager productivity ramp, and the concentration of these new hires in a subset of our regions." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • "In February, this payer implemented AI-based prior authorization tools" and management said its largest Medicare Advantage payer saw its 30-day approval rate fall "to roughly 25%," then recover to "approximately 40%" before falling "back below 30%." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • "In May of 2026, we received a civil investigative demand from the U.S. Department of Justice related to certain sales and marketing practices as described in our 10-Q. We are fully cooperating with the investigation." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • "For the full year of 2026, we now expect total revenue between $58 million and $60 million." (Chief Financial Officer Jared Oasheim)

Outlook

  • "For the full year of 2026, we now expect total revenue between $58 million and $60 million." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "We now expect full year gross margin between 86% and 87%." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "We now expect operating expenses to be between $99 million and $101 million." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "For the third quarter of 2026, we expect to report total revenue between $13.5 million and $14.5 million." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "Based on the current tenure of our team, and as we focus on driving productivity in our existing territories, we are not anticipating adding any more sales territories for the balance of the year." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)

Financial Results

  • "Total revenue was $15.7 million, an increase of $2.1 million, or 16%." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "Revenue in the U.S. was $14.8 million" and "revenue units in the U.S. totaled 466 compared to 391." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "Revenue in Europe was $0.9 million, a decrease of $0.4 million, or 31%" and "total revenue units in Europe decreased to 40 from 61." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "Gross profit was $13.7 million" and "gross margin increased to 87% compared to 84% a year ago." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "SG&A expenses increased $0.3 million, or 1%, to $23.6 million" and management attributed this primarily to "non-cash, stock-based compensation expenses and legal expenses." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • "Net loss was $14 million, or $0.53 per share" and "as of June 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $64.6 million." (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)

Q&A

  • Max Kruszeski, William Blair: Asked whether turnover was abnormal and how far along rep ramps are; President, CEO & Director Hykes said turnover over the last 18 months was "higher than we would have liked" and that the problem is "concentrated in a handful of regions" with "our least tenured leaders."
  • Max Kruszeski, William Blair: Asked about center adds after "only added one since Q1"; Chief Financial Officer Oasheim said the company is "focused on driving deeper adoption within the centers that are active" and that without new territories, "it's unlikely we'd see net growth in that center number for the balance of the year."
  • Chase Knickerbocker, Craig-Hallum: Asked for a rep cohort view; President, CEO & Director Hykes contrasted "strong double digits consistently" in stable regions versus regions with turnover "well north of 50% in some cases" where the company is seeing "negative implant growth rates year-to-date."
  • Chase Knickerbocker, Craig-Hallum: Asked what drove lower OpEx guidance; Chief Financial Officer Oasheim said the reduction was "partially" tied to the lower revenue outlook, plus spending pullbacks "within marketing and development areas" to redeploy resources to sales productivity.
  • Robert Marcus, JPMorgan: Challenged whether this is demand vs. execution after multiple years in a similar revenue band and asked about cash needs; President, CEO & Director Hykes responded, "our problem today is in fact execution" and "that is fixable"; Chief Financial Officer Oasheim said the company believes it has "at least 18 months of cash" and "$40 million remains undrawn under our debt facility."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative, with JPMorgan pressing, "are you coming to a point where it's not an execution issue but more a demand issue?" (Robert Marcus, JPMorgan)
  • Management: slightly defensive in Q&A but assertive on causality, stating "our problem today is in fact execution" and "we are going to fix it." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • Versus last quarter: management’s tone shifted from "a strong start to the year" and confidence in maintaining "this cadence of expansion" to acknowledging "we've lowered our revenue guidance" and "we are not satisfied with the outlook for the balance of the year." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance language moved from "we continue to expect total revenue between $63 million and $67 million" in Q1 to "we now expect total revenue between $58 million and $60 million" in Q2. (Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • Commercial posture shifted from expecting to "maintain this cadence of expansion" in territories and centers (Q1) to "not anticipating adding any more sales territories for the balance of the year" and prioritizing productivity fixes (Q2). (President, CEO & Director Hykes; Chief Financial Officer Oasheim)
  • Reimbursement narrative sharpened from a broad, industry-wide "new administrative dynamic" in Q1 to Q2’s emphasis on a single "largest Medicare Advantage payer" whose approval rate fell "back below 30%." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • New headline risk emerged in Q2 with the DOJ civil investigative demand disclosure, which was not discussed in Q1. (President, CEO & Director Hykes)

Risks and Concerns

  • "We are seeing signs that the back half of the year will not be as strong as the first" and management linked this to sales turnover, slower rep ramps, and regional leadership gaps. (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • "We continue to be challenged by the change in behavior from our largest Medicare Advantage payer" and management said physicians have become "more hesitant" for patients covered by that plan. (President, CEO & Director Hykes)
  • "We received a civil investigative demand from the U.S. Department of Justice related to certain sales and marketing practices" and management said it is "fully cooperating." (President, CEO & Director Hykes)

Final Takeaway

Management characterized the quarter as operationally mixed: $15.7 million in Q2 revenue with 87% gross margin, but a lowered 2026 revenue outlook of $58 million to $60 million tied to concentrated sales-force turnover and slower productivity ramps, compounded by renewed friction at its largest Medicare Advantage payer where 30-day approvals were described as falling back below 30%. Alongside commercial and reimbursement actions—expanded onboarding, new field roles funded through reallocation, and a pause on adding U.S. territories—management also disclosed receipt of a DOJ civil investigative demand and highlighted liquidity messaging of at least 18 months of cash and $40 million undrawn debt capacity.

data.title: Runway Growth appoints Michael Rovner as co-CEO
data.description:
• Runway Growth (RWAY) said on Friday it appointed Michael Rovner as co-chief executive officer and also as co-chief investment officer, alongside founder David Spreng.
  • Rovner joins from BC Partners, where he was a managing director following its 2023 acquisition of Ovation Partners, the growth capital business he co-founded. The appointment comes as Runway expands its financing platform for growth-stage companies.
